media.alt: One in every three Pakistanis is hypertensive

content.text: "One in every three Pakistanis is hypertensive and Pakistani children have higher mean blood pressure compared to the rest of the world," this was stated by Dr Seema Ameen Mohammad at a seminar held to mark the World Health Day on April 6. The seminar titled "Family Medicine for All" was organised by the Aga Khan University (AKU).

Dr Mohammad, lecturer and consultant Family Medicine at AKU, informed the audience about the latest trends in management of hypertension. She said that every year, 7.1 million people die of high blood pressure. The treatment of hypertension is associated with 40% reduction in the risk of stroke and 15% reduction in the risk of Myocardial Infarction.

Dr. Bader Sabir Ali, Associate Professor Department of Family Medicine, revealed that two-third of the 360 million people suffering from depression worldwide, live in the developing countries. She referred to a prevalence study done in the Qayumabad area of Karachi where 30% of women were found suffering from depression and every fourth person coming for a consultation was suffering from some kind of depression. She said that depression was likely to be the second most prevalent disease by 2020, surpassed only by cardiovascular disease.

Dr Marie Andrades, Asssistant Professor and Consultant Family Physician, elaborated on the Well Child Care programme and stressed on regular visits to the family physicians for assessing and monitoring the growth and nurturing of the baby.

Dr Raheem Dhanani, Assistant Professor and Consultant Family Physician, spoke about the role of family physicians in occupational health and stressed the importance of proper training and education in Family Medicine for improving the state of occupational health in Pakistan.

Prof Riaz Qureshi, Professor and Chairman Department of Family Medicine at AKU, highlighted the direct as well as the indirect health hazards faced by physicians during their professional duties. He stressed the need for preventive measures and healthy lifestyles for doctors so that they could set examples for their patients.

As a part of its social responsibility and commitment to the advancement of health research and education, AKU regularly holds seminars, symposiums and such events to increase awareness on health and education related issues which are of national importance.
